definition: When evaluation or benchmark data inadvertently appears in a model's training dataset, inflating apparent performance on that benchmark.
details: Data contamination is a significant concern for evaluating web-scale-trained LLMs, since benchmark questions and answers may have been scraped into training corpora, undermining the validity of reported benchmark scores.
story: Think of a referee whose job is to be completely honest about who touched the ball last. Before trusting a machine, someone has to measure how good it really is — fairly and honestly. It is the exam that separates “it sounds good” from “it actually is good”. What gets measured is what actually gets better. That shared ruler is Data Contamination.
